title: 04. BM25 & Lexical Search: Probabilistic Retrieval Model
summary: The probabilistic retrieval model formalises relevance as a probability. Given query Q, the goal is to estimate P(R=1 | D, Q) — the probability that document D is relevant to query Q.

sections.title: ① Concept Explanation
sections.body:
The probabilistic retrieval model formalises relevance as a probability. Given query Q, the goal is to estimate P(R=1 | D, Q) — the probability that document D is relevant to query Q. The Binary Independence Model (BIM), the foundation of BM25, assumes terms are independently distributed and models P(t|R=1) (probability of term appearing in relevant documents) vs P(t|R=0) (in non-relevant documents). The relevance score is derived as a log-odds ratio, which naturally produces the IDF-like and TF-like components seen in BM25.

$$\text{score}(D,Q) = \sum_{t \in Q} \log \frac{P(t=1|R=1)}{P(t=1|R=0)} + \log \frac{P(t=0|R=1)}{P(t=0|R=0)}$$

sections.title: ④ Visual Explanation
sections.body:
```
PROBABILISTIC MODEL — SCORE DERIVATION
══════════════════════════════════════════════════

  For each query term t:
  
  P(t in doc | doc is RELEVANT)   =  p_t   (high for important terms)
  P(t in doc | doc NOT relevant)  =  u_t   (low for discriminating terms)
  
  Log-odds weight:
       ┌─────────────────────────────┐
  w_t =│ log [ p_t(1-u_t) / u_t(1-p_t) ] │
       └─────────────────────────────┘
  
  Without relevance feedback: p_t ≈ 0.5, u_t = df/N
  ∴ w_t ≈ log(N/df)  ←─── This IS the IDF!
  
  Final score = Σ w_t  (sum over query terms present in doc)
              = Σ IDF(t)  ← BIM score
              
  BM25 adds TF component:
              = Σ IDF(t) × TF_saturated(t, D)
```

quiz.question: What is the Robertson-Spärck Jones relevance weight (RSJ weight)?
options: (1) No relevance info → use RSJ with uniform priors. (2) After user interaction, collect R relevant docs → re-estimate P(t|R=1).
With |V|=1M dimensions and most entries being 0, vectors are extremely sparse.

When no relevance info is available, this simplifies to the classic IDF.
quiz.explanation: The log-odds ratio of a term appearing in relevant vs non-relevant documents: $$w_t = \log \frac{(r_t + 0.5)(N - n_t - R + r_t + 0.5)}{(n_t - r_t + 0.5)(R - r_t + 0.5)}$$ Where: N=total docs, n_t=docs containing term, R=relevant docs, r_t=relevant docs containing term. When no relevance info is available, this simplifies to the classic IDF.

quiz.question: What is the Binary Independence Model (BIM)?
options: An information need is the underlying intent ("I want to understand BM25 tuning").
I do not recommend this product" and "I recommend this product" have nearly identical BoW representations.
Instead of P(Q|D), score documents by -KL(θ_Q || θ_D) — the KL divergence from the query LM to the document LM.
Assumes: (1) terms are binary (present/absent), (2) terms are independent, (3) relevance is binary.
quiz.explanation: Assumes: (1) terms are binary (present/absent), (2) terms are independent, (3) relevance is binary. Under these assumptions, the optimal ranking is by the RSJ weight sum. BM25 relaxes the binary term assumption to include term frequency.

quiz.question: How does BM25 extend BIM?
options: (1) Word order and syntax — "not good" vs "good" are different in meaning but similar in BoW.
When the presence/absence of key terms is the primary relevance signal.
Retrieve posting lists for each term, then intersect them. Use the shortest posting list first to minimise work.
BIM treats term occurrence as binary (0/1). BM25 adds: (1) term frequency (TF) component with saturation via k1, (2) document length normalisation via b.
quiz.explanation: BIM treats term occurrence as binary (0/1). BM25 adds: (1) term frequency (TF) component with saturation via k1, (2) document length normalisation via b. This makes BM25 a "BM" (Best Match) extension of BIM.

quiz.question: What does the 0.5 smoothing constant in BM25 IDF prevent?
options: Use bigrams or trigrams as additional dimensions. Or use positional VSM where phrase terms get boosted weights when they co-occur within a window.
An information need is the underlying intent ("I want to understand BM25 tuning").
Either TF=0 (term doesn't appear in the document) or IDF=0 (term appears in every document and is thus useless for discrimination).
Division by zero and log(0). IDF(t) = log((N - df + 0.5)/(df + 0.5) + 1) — the +0.5 Laplace smoothing ensures every term has a non-zero, non-infinite IDF.
quiz.explanation: Division by zero and log(0). IDF(t) = log((N - df + 0.5)/(df + 0.5) + 1) — the +0.5 Laplace smoothing ensures every term has a non-zero, non-infinite IDF.

quiz.question: Why is the probabilistic model better than VSM for relevance estimation?
options: Dot product favours longer documents because they have larger magnitude vectors.
Products of small probabilities underflow to zero numerically.
(1) All-or-nothing — no partial matching. (2) Query formulation burden on user.
VSM is a geometric model with no probabilistic justification.
quiz.explanation: VSM is a geometric model with no probabilistic justification. The probabilistic model has a clear generative story: documents are sampled from relevant/non-relevant distributions, giving a principled framework for combining evidence.
